The FAA must receive comments on the proposed airworthiness directive by January 4, 2027.

The proposed AD would require a one-time inspection of the tail rotor control system and, depending on results, corrective actions, as well as revision of the aircraft maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness.

The FAA estimates the proposed AD would affect 289 helicopters of U.S. registry, with an estimated cost of $340 per helicopter for the tail rotor control system inspection and $85 per helicopter for maintenance program revision.
The FAA has proposed a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) models due to incomplete inspection instructions after a hard landing.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: The National Park Service has issued a final rule amending special regulations for Mammoth Cave National Park to expand recreational opportunities. Under this new directive, visitors will be permitted to use bicycles on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails across the park. The amendment also authorizes horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, which is currently closed to equestrians. These changes implement a preferred alternative from a comprehensive land and river trails plan finalized in December 2024. The updated regulations are scheduled to become effective on December 21, 2026.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: The National Park Service final rule for Mammoth Cave National Park is effective December 21, 2026, and allows bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails.
The rule allows visitors to ride horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, expanding equestrian opportunities in the park.
Under the preferred alternative, the NPS will add approximately 66 miles of land-based trails to the park trail system, representing a 72 percent increase in trail mileage.

The rule adds eight new trails for bicycle use, including Brooks Knob Road Cemetery Trail, Brooks Knob Road Trail, Crystal Cave Road Trail, East Entrance Trail, Little Hope Cemetery Trail, Sugar Sink Connector Trail, Sugar Sink Trail, and West Entrance Trail.

In December 2024, the Regional Director for Interior Region 2, South Atlantic—Gulf, signed a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) selecting the preferred alternative from the Environmental Assessment.
The final rule opens the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road to horseback riding.
